title: Configuration and Options in ASP.NET Core
summary: Assumes basic dependency injection: compose configuration providers and give consumers typed, validated settings.
objectives: Explain how later configuration providers can override earlier values.
Explain why strongly typed options improve maintainability.

reviewCandidates.prompt: Why prefer strongly typed options over scattered configuration keys?
reviewCandidates.answer: They group meaningful settings behind an explicit dependency and centralize binding/validation, making consumers easier to refactor and test.

reviewCandidates.prompt: How are duplicate configuration keys resolved across ASP.NET Core providers?
reviewCandidates.answer: The provider added later takes precedence for that key. The actual configured provider order determines the winning value.

reviewCandidates.prompt: How do IOptions and IOptionsSnapshot differ conceptually?
reviewCandidates.answer: IOptions supplies a cached value without reload updates. IOptionsSnapshot caches per scope, so a later request scope can use updated values when the underlying provider supports reload.
